title: Build the Pipeline First, Then Fill It With Revenue
documentTitle: United States v. Google LLC (Ad Tech) — Email from Joan Braddi to Neal Mohan et al. on Display Strategy
excerptForBlog:
Thanks again for making the time to meet re: our display ads strategy today. A few follow-up notes:

Current State of product strategy (three pillars):

a) Platform to ACCESS the desired inventory. I think we have both the strategy as well as detailed roadmap figured out. We also completed a detailed pricing review and refresh across all products.

b) Ad Exchange to AGGREGATE the inventory that the platform piece gives us access to. Here I think we have the strategy (including positioning to advertisers and publishers) and the roadmap features and timing mostly figured out. One major component we are working on is AdX pricing.

c) Google Content Network to MONETIZE the inventory we aggregate via Ad Exchange and all our AdSense deals. Here we believe that our high level strategy is in place (focus on performance: targeting and optimization) but the roadmap is NOT ready yet. We are working hard on this part and hope to have an initial plan covering the first half of 2009 in place in the next few weeks. It is my highest priority across all the elements of the display strategy.

Based on Omid's feedback, one of the items I am preparing is a quarter-by-quarter review that will include: detailed roadmap for each pillar; our positioning and value proposition to advertisers and publishers; and suggested specific objectives related to display for that quarter.

lessonTitle: Build the Pipeline First, Then Fill It With Revenue
pullQuote: The smartest strategy documents don't just show where you're winning — they name exactly where the work isn't done yet.
leadershipTraits: Thinks in sequences, not just goals
Moves fast when the gap is named
situation: On September 3, 2008, Google executive Joan Braddi sent a follow-up memo to Neal Mohan and others after a meeting on Google's display advertising strategy. The memo maps out three interlocking product pillars and honestly flags which pieces are ready and which are not. The stakes: Google was trying to build an end-to-end display advertising business — from accessing inventory, to aggregating it, to monetizing it.
insight: The three pillars Braddi names — Access, Aggregate, Monetize — are not independent bets. They are a sequential chain. You can't monetize inventory you haven't aggregated; you can't aggregate what you haven't accessed. This is vertical integration logic applied to a marketplace. Each layer creates leverage for the next. What makes the memo strategically sharp is its honesty about where the chain breaks. Braddi writes plainly that the monetization layer — the Google Content Network roadmap — is 'NOT ready yet' and calls it her 'highest priority across all the elements.' She isn't hiding the gap; she's naming it so it gets fixed first. That's the hidden move: before escalating to senior leadership (she mentions preparing a quarter-by-quarter review based on 'Omid's feedback'), she locks down exactly where the weakness sits. You go upstairs with a diagnosis, not just a status update.
application: Draw your own three-pillar chain for whatever you're building — acquisition, conversion, retention; sourcing, production, distribution. Then be as explicit as Braddi: write down which pillar has a finished roadmap, which is mostly figured out, and which is 'NOT ready yet.' That last one becomes your number-one priority this week, before you present the strategy to anyone above you.
